note.title: 2–1–2 adjectives
note.overview: Adjectives agree with their nouns in case, number and gender. Agreement does not require identical endings: nauta bonus is masculine nominative singular.
learningGoals: Recall the taught forms and facts independently.
Apply them to translation and GCSE-style questions.
Use the answer and individual mark points to improve precision.
summary: Adjectives agree with their nouns in case, number and gender. Agreement does not require identical endings: nauta bonus is masculine nominative singular.
The masculine and neuter follow second-declension endings; the feminine follows first-declension endings. Neuter nominative and accusative always match and their plural ends in -a.
Pulcher loses its stem e in pulchra; miser keeps its e in misera. Forms may be ambiguous without context: magna templa is neuter nominative or accusative plural.
mustMemoriseRules: Adjectives agree with their nouns in case, number and gender. Agreement does not require identical endings: nauta bonus is masculine nominative singular.
The masculine and neuter follow second-declension endings; the feminine follows first-declension endings. Neuter nominative and accusative always match and their plural ends in -a.
Pulcher loses its stem e in pulchra; miser keeps its e in misera. Forms may be ambiguous without context: magna templa is neuter nominative or accusative plural.
detailedExplanation: Adjectives agree with their nouns in case, number and gender. Agreement does not require identical endings: nauta bonus is masculine nominative singular.
The masculine and neuter follow second-declension endings; the feminine follows first-declension endings. Neuter nominative and accusative always match and their plural ends in -a.
Pulcher loses its stem e in pulchra; miser keeps its e in misera. Forms may be ambiguous without context: magna templa is neuter nominative or accusative plural.
